 Chapter 1. About the documentation

l  Words, abbreviations, and other terms that are used on their own, such as 'Developer Mode, J1', are listed in 'Appendix 1. Glossary and Description ' in case of confusion

l  DG Manager and the SDK have been tested in a Windows 10 x64, Ubuntu 24.04 x64, Ubuntu 22.04 x64, C++20 environment and are also compatible with similar OS environments. Additionally, they have been verified to run on the following PC specifications
    * CPU: AMD Ryzen 5 5600 6-Core Processor
    * RAM: 16GB
    * Graphic: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060

l  The Operator Mode communication protocols are 'Modbus RTU' and 'Modbus TCP'. Developer Mode uses its own protocol based on TCP/IP

 

Chapter 2.Precautions

l  Depending on your PC performance and network environment, the program may not work smoothly.

l  DG Manager can be used to operate the DG-1F-M, DG-2F-M, DG-3F-B, DG-3F-M, DG-4F-M, and DG-5F. However, please note that different firmware and gripper models support different functions, so please pay attention to the firmware and model when using DG Manager.

l  Failure to follow the instructions in this manual and incorrect operation may result in malfunctions. This may cause damage to the gripper and in some cases may not be covered by the after-sales service.

l  If you need any other support, please contact Tesollo Support (support@tesollo.com )

Chapter 3. Getting started

3.1 Installing DG Manager

3.1.1 Installation file location

3.1.1.1 Windows

Inside the USB drive included in the gripper packaging, navigate to the folder path shown in the illustration: “Software - DGManager.” There, you will find an installation file named “DGManagerInstaller_ver_x_x_x.exe” (where ver_x_x_x indicates the version of DG Manager). Run this installation file to install DG Manager.

3.1.1.2 Ubuntu 24.04 / 22.04

Inside the USB drive included in the gripper packaging, navigate to the folder path shown in the illustration: “Software – DGManager-Linux.” There, you will find an installation file named “DGManager_linux_ver_x_x_x.zip” (where ver_x_x_x indicates the version of DG Manager). You can run DGManager after extracting the archive.

 

3.1.2 Installing DG Manager

3.1.2.1 Windows

When you run the program, the installation file screen is displayed as shown above. Click 'Next>' to go to the next screen.

After setting the file path, start the installation. Make sure you have enough free space on your storage before starting the installation.

 Item

Number

Item

Description

1

Destination Folder Browse

Set the path to the folder where you want to install the files

2

Check capacity

Displaying file size and install space capacity

3

Install

Start installing files

When the file installation is successfully completed, a screen like the one above will appear, and a shortcut to DGManager.exe will be created on the desktop.

3.1.2.2 Ubuntu 24.04 / 22.04

Example

bash

# Extract the compressed file

unzip DGManager_linux_ver_1_2_0.zip  

# Enter the extracted directory

cd DGManager-linux-x64/

# Install dependencies, set execution permissions, and run

. install_run.sh

# Grant execution permissions and run (without installing libraries)

. run.sh

# Execute the program
./DGManager

 

After extracting the archive, you can run DGManager.

If you need to install dependency packages and set execution permissions, please run the install_run.sh script first.
(This process requires an internet connection.)

If you only need to grant execution permission and run the program without installing libraries, run the run.sh script.

To simply execute the program, run the ./DGManager file directly.

 

3.2 Deleting DG Manager

3.2.1.1 Windows

Enter the file installation path and you will find a file named 'UninstallDGManager.exe'. Run that file to start uninstalling the DG Manager program.

 When the file removal is complete, you'll see a screen like the one shown above.

3.2.1.2 Ubuntu 24.04 / 22.04

Since the files are shared as a ZIP archive, you can simply delete the extracted directory to remove all files on Linux.

 

Chapter 4. Communication Connection Screen

4.1 Login Screen

4.1.1 Screen layout

Description

Delto Gripper supports Operator Mode and Developer Mode.

Operator Mode

This mode allows control using the internal controller of the product. It supports the Modbus Protocol, enabling easy control of the gripper either by simply modifying the register map or using the provided UI.

If you are using User Mode and the SDK, you must set the “Torque limit mode” to “off” in order to use “stall torque.”

Developer Mode

This mode uses a user-developed controller that receives information from each joint of the gripper and allows you to control each joint directly.

* Caution

Using 'Torque Limit Mode' off in Operator Mode or using stall torque in Developer Mode may cause a rapid increase in product temperature and potential product damage. Please note that repairs (A/S) may be difficult in case of failure.

4.1.2 Operator Mode Connection

4.1.2.1 Set up a Modbus RTU Connection

Description

Modbus RTU Connection Example

If the gripper model you are connecting is DG-3F-M using Modbus RTU via the COM8 port, with a baud rate of 115200 and Slave ID 1, first select “Delto Gripper-3F-M” under “Model.” Then select “Modbus RTU,” click the Scan button, choose “COM8” under “Serial Port,” select “115,200” under “Baudrate,” and enter 1 for “Slave ID.” Finally, click the CONNECT button. If the communication is successfully established, the system will proceed to the main screen.

4.1.2.2 Set up a Modbus TCP Connection

Description

Example Modbus TCP Connection

If the gripper model you are connecting is DG-3F-M, with the IP address set to 169.254.186.72, port 502, and Slave ID 1, first select “Delto Gripper-3F-M” under “Model.” Then select “Modbus TCP” and enter the corresponding values in the fields below. Enter “169.254.186.72” for “IP,” “502” for “PORT,” and “1” for “Slave ID.”

Finally, click the “CONNECT” button. If the communication is successfully established, the system will proceed to the main screen.

4.2 Main screen

4.2.1 Screen layout

 Description

The main screen allows you to access the full range of functions for the gripper. 

You can turn gripper control on or off, and monitor real-time joint angle information through a 3D simulation. Additionally, you can preview and execute motions using recipes, and access various advanced settings such as theme switching, disconnecting, and viewing information. The gripper can be easily controlled through the “Start/Stop Gripper System” section on the main screen.  When in the “Ready” state, selecting “Start” activates the system and prepares it to receive commands.  When in the “Running” state, selecting “Stop” halts the gripper’s operation and ends control.

Chapter 5. Monitoring screens

5.1 Screen layout

 Description

The Monitoring screen provides a real-time display of selected graph items and the ability to save data. You can select joints, current, velocity, and temperature to view in a real-time graph, set the horizontal range (number of data to save) and vertical range of the graph, select the joints to display on the graph, and save the current graph data as a CSV file or image PNG file.

6.1.3 Setting up grasp data

 Description

This feature allows you to configure the gripper’s grasping data. It is only available for the DG-2F-M, DG-3F-B, DG-3F-M, DG-4F-M, and DG-5F models. Each model provides its own Grasping Algorithm. By default, the real-time force control grasping algorithm is enabled. This algorithm allows each fingertip involved in the grasp to follow the center between the fingers. Because it operates in real time, even if an external force causes the joint positions to change, the gripper will attempt to maintain the grasping posture based on the new joint positions.

[Maintain grasp posture at current position

even if gripper joint position changes]

Item

Number

Name

Description

1

Grasping Algorithm

See 9.2.9 enum DG_GRASP_MODE

2

Force

Set grasp strength (unit: N)

Note

11.1 Grasp Setup Functions

* Available series: DG-2F-M, DG-3F-B, DG-3F-M, DG-4F-M, DG-5F

* See 'Appendix 2. Error list' for errors

 

6.1.4 Setting the Position Control Mode

Description

Joints set to Position Control mode will perform position control instead of grasping when performing a grasp. This is used when you do not want to move a particular joint during a grasp.

If you check J1 and J2 and then perform a grasp on ' 6.1.2 Grasp operations ', then joint 1 and joint 2 will be excluded from the grasp algorithm and will only perform a translate to the target position value.

6.2.2 Position Control

Description

Position control Motion is the ability to reposition the joints of the gripper. To perform a position move, you need to set a target value. The unit of the target value is 'degree'. You can also set the time to travel to the target when moving the position. The unit of travel time is 'ms'.

If the Time of J1 is entered as 1000ms and the degree value is entered as 60º, the first joint corresponding to J1 will move from the current position to 60º in 1000ms. The 'Time' you set here may not be an exact number depending on the performance of the controller when used in Developer Mode and may not be an exact number depending on the current control value for the joint.

(Unit: ms)

6.2.3 Teaching mode

Description

Teach mode is a feature that allows you to teach the gripper directly. The operator can teach the gripper by entering target values for the gripper joints, or the operator can utilize Teach Mode to perform teaching through direct instruction. When the 'Activate' button is selected to use Teach Mode, the gripper will enter the Teach Mode state and the user can physically manipulate the gripper to move it to the desired position. This is useful for creating recipe poses that save the current position.

6.3.2 Setting the Gain Mode

Description

The Gain Mode setting allows you to set the PD, PID control mode. The Delto Gripper Series operates in PD control by default. This is because it allows the object and gripper to react flexibly to physical damage in collision situations. On the other hand, for higher positioning accuracy, we recommend using PID control mode.

8.1.3 Joint Offset

Description

Joint offset settings are used to define the joint’s zero position in software when the physical position of a joint is misaligned. If a specific joint deviates from the zero pose when the gripper is moved to the zero position, manually align the joint to the correct zero pose, then record the change in position as the joint offset.

Item

Number

Name

Description

1

(unit: degree)

2

Apply the configured Joint Offset, Joint Inpose, and Moving Inpose all at once

Note

10.1.2 SetGripperOption

* See 'Appendix 2. Error list' for errors

 

 

8.1.4 Joint Inpose

 Description

Joint Inpose is a range-setting feature used to determine whether each joint has reached its target position. For example, if Joint 1 (J1) is set to a tolerance of 3 degrees and the current joint position is 30 degrees, then a target position of 60 degrees will be considered “reached” once the joint reaches 57 degrees.

This feature is particularly useful when performing continuous position movements, allowing the next operation to begin even before the joint has fully reached its target.

Apply the setting by clicking the “Apply” button under section 8.1.3 Joint Offset.

Item

Number

Name

Description

1

J1 - Jn Inpose

Set the J1 to J20 joint arrival check range

(unit: degree)

Note

10.1.2 SetGripperOption

* See 'Appendix 2. Error list' for errors

 

 

8.1.5 Moving Inpose

Moving Inpose is a feature that sets a range for checking joint movement. If the Inpose value is 1 degree, the joint is considered to have moved if the amount of change in the joint is more than 1 degree. Press the “Apply button” in section 8.1.3 Joint Offset to apply the settings.

8.2.4 Experiments

Description

Experiments can use experimental functions. For a detailed description, see Chapter 14 Experimental Functions. This feature is supported differently depending on the gripper model.

8.2.4.1 Inhand Manipulation

How to use

First, press the 'NEXT' button once to go to 'Step1'. Before performing Inhand Manipulation, a grasp must be performed first, so press 'GRASP' 2 times to perform a grasp. If a grasp is not performed, the 'NEXT' button will not be activated. Press 'NEXT' to go to 'Step2'.

In 'Step2', set the Gain value. Depending on the gain value, the Motion of Inhand Manipulation may change. Therefore, it is necessary to enter the appropriate gain value according to the coordinate value you want to move. After entering the gain value, press 'SET' to activate 'NEXT'. After pressing 'NEXT', you will be taken to 'Step3', where you will enter a value relative to the coordinates you want to move. If you enter 20 for x, you will move 20mm on the x-axis. When you finished entering the coordinates, press 'NEXT' to move to 'Step4'.

 

In 'Step4', set the Inhand Manipulation action time. If the value of 9 is entered as 1000 (ms), the Inhand Manipulation will be operated over 1000 ms. After entering, press 'NEXT' to move to the last screen. Finally, press 'RUN' button 11 to execute Inhand Manipulation. If the Inhand Manipulation Motion does not move as expected, compensate by setting the 'Step2' gain value.

9.2.9 enum DG_GRASP_MODE

Enumeration constants for setting the gripper grasp mode.

DG_GRASP_MODE_2F is only available for the DG-2F-M model.

DG_GRASP_MODE_3F is only available for DG-3F-B and DG-3F-M models.

DG_GRASP_MODE_4F is only available for the DG-4F-M model.

DG_GRASP_MODE_5F is only available for the DG-5F model.

Chapter 10. System functions

10.1 System Settings Functions

10.1.1 SetGripperSystem

Description

This function is used to input the configuration values required to establish communication with the gripper. It must be executed first; if this function is not performed, no other functions can be executed.

Parameter

Data Types

Variables

Description

struct

GripperSystemSetting

9.3.3 struct GripperSystemSetting

Returns

Number

Value

Description

0

DG_RESULT_NONE

Normal

If it is not zero

ERROR

Appendix 2 Error list

Example

C/C++

                // For Operator Mode Modbus RTU connection

                  GripperSystemSetting setting;

                  setting.communicationMode = COMMUNICATION_MODE_RS485;

                  setting.controlMode = CONTROL_MODE_OPERATOR;

                  char port[MAX_COMPORT_NAME_SIZE] = "COM1";    // Connectable comfort input

                  memcpy(setting.comport, port, MAX_COMPORT_NAME_SIZE);

                  setting.baudrate = 115200;    // Enter the baudrate set in the gripper

                  setting.slaveID = 1;    // Enter the Slave ID set on the gripper

                  DG_RESULT result = SetGripperSystem(setting);

 

                  // For Operator Mode Modbus TCP connection

                  GripperSystemSetting setting;

                  setting.communicationMode = COMMUNICATION_MODE_ ETHERNET;

                  setting.controlMode = CONTROL_MODE_OPERATOR;

                  char ip[MAX_GRIPPER_IP_ADDRESS_SIZE] = "169.254.186.72";    // // Enter the gripper IP address

                  memcpy(setting.ip, ip, MAX_GRIPPER_IP_ADDRESS_SIZE);

                  setting.port = 502;     // Enter the Port set in the gripper

                  setting.slaveID = 1;    // Enter the Slave ID set on the gripper

                  DG_RESULT result = SetGripperSystem(setting);

 

                  // For developer mode TCP/IP connections

                  GripperSystemSetting setting;

                  setting.communicationMode = COMMUNICATION_MODE_ETHERNET;

                  setting.controlMode = CONTROL_MODE_DEVELOPER_MODE;

                  char ip[MAX_GRIPPER_IP_ADDRESS_SIZE] = "169.254.186.72";    // // Enter the gripper IP address

                  memcpy(setting.ip, ip, MAX_GRIPPER_IP_ADDRESS_SIZE);

                  setting.port = 502;    // Enter the Port set in the gripper

                  setting.slaveID = 1;    // Enter the Slave ID set on the gripper

                  DG_RESULT result = SetGripperSystem(setting);

10.1.2 SetGripperOption

Description

Options to set default values for gripper motion. If this option is not selected, you will not be able to control the gripper.

Parameter

Data Types

Variables

Description

struct

GripperSystemSetting

9.3.4 struct GripperSetting

Returns

Number

Value

Description

0

DG_RESULT_NONE

Normal

If it is not zero

ERROR

Appendix 2 Error list

Example

C/C++

                  // When setting up the DG-3F-M

                  float offset[MAX_NUM_JOINT] = { 0 };

                  float inpose[MAX_NUM_JOINT] = { 0 };

                  GripperSetting gs;

                  offset[0] = 2; // offset joint 1 by 2 degrees

                  inpose[2] = 3; // Set the 3rd joint inpose 3 degrees

                  gs.model = DG_MODEL_DG_3F_M; // set gripper model

                  memcpy(gs.jointOffset, offset, sizeof(offset));

                  memcpy(gs.jointInpose, offset, sizeof(inpose));

                  gs.movingInpose = 0.3;

                  DG_RESULT result = SetGripperOption(gs);

10.2.4 CallbackForOnCommunicationPeriod

Description

Receive the communication cycles with the gripper. This value represents the number of times the gripper and PC communicate back and forth in one second. Depending on the specifications of the controller associated with the gripper, this value may be lower, and if it is, smooth control may not occur.

This function is only available in Developer Mode.

 

Parameter

Data Types

Variables

Description

int

period

Communication cycles

Returns

Number

Value

Description

0

DG_RESULT_NONE

Normal

If it is not zero

ERROR

Appendix 2 Error list

Example

C/C++

                  static void OnCountPeriod(const int period)

{

                      if (period <  MINIMUM_CONTROL_PERIOD)

                      {

                          std::cout<< "low communication period"<< endl;

                      }

}

        DG_RESULT result =   CallbackForOnCommunicationPeriod(*OnCountPeriod);

Chapter 11. Motion Setting Functions

11.1 Grasp Setup Functions

Sets the grasp algorithm based on force control. It provides grasp modes including five-fingered, three-fingered, two-fingered, parallel, and enveloping, and allows the use of grasp options, position control modes, and more to perform grasp actions in various ways.

11.1.1 SetGraspData

Description

To perform a grasp, you set up the grasp data.

                  int graspMode = DG_GRASP_MODE_5F_5FINGER; // three-finger focus grasp mode

                  float graspForce = 3.0;

                  int graspOption = GRASP_OPTION_NONE; // no grasp option

                  int smoothGraspping = IS_ON; // use smooth grasping

                  DG_RESULT result = SetGraspData(graspMode, graspForce, graspOption, smoothGrasping);

11.4 Setting Gain I

Sets the gripper I-gain and error integral maximum. I gain is the gain you set to reduce error and make it sensitive to small changes to reach the target value precisely. A high value of I Gain reacts quickly to error but can cause the gripper to jitter, while a low value slows down error compensation and delays recovery of the error integral value, which can cause vibration. The error integral maximum value serves to prevent the error integral value from accumulating rapidly; too low a value may not compensate for the error sufficiently, and too high a value may slow the recovery of the error integral value.

The I gain continues to accumulate the control signal until the error reaches zero. Therefore, in situations where the gripper cannot recover from the error on its own, failure due to joint overload can occur. Therefore, precise tuning to the proper value is required for stable control and care must be taken when using it.

11.6 Setting the motion time

Sets the time for the gripper to reach the target position. The shorter the action time, the faster the motion; the longer the action time, the slower the motion. If the action time is set very low, the gripper moves at full speed. This feature only applies to position control. The behavior of the action time may vary depending on the controller specifications. The SDK uses an internal timer to manage the action time, but if the controller environment using the SDK is not optimal, the internal timer's accuracy cannot be guaranteed. Additionally, movement during the action time depends on the gripper settings, so very low action times may not be reliable.

                  int controlPIDMode = 0; // set PID control mode

                  int recipeNumber = 1; // set recipe number

                  DG_RESULT result = SetJointGainPIDAllEqual(P, D, I, iLimit);

                  if (result == DG_RESULT_NONE) result = SetControlPIDMode(controlPIDMode);

                  if (result == DG_RESULT_NONE) result = UpdateRecipeGainData(recipeNumber);

Note

Chapter 14. Experimental Functions

This chapter introduces experimental functions using the Delto Gripper. The experimental functions are supported only in Developer Mode on the DG-3F-B and DG-3F-M models. Since these experimental functions are not officially released features, expected behaviors may not be performed at certain settings or positions. Nevertheless, these functions allow you to experience the unique characteristics of the Delto Gripper.

14.7.1 SetManipulationGainPIDAll

Description

Set the P, I, D gains and error integral maximums for inhand manipulation Motion. Sets the gains for the position components X, Y, and Z in the Cartesian coordinate system. This feature is only supported by DG-3F-B and DG-3F-M.

Parameter

Data Types

Variables

Description

ERROR

Example

C/C++

                  float P[CARTESIAN_COORDINATE_POSE_COUNT / 2 * MAX_FINGER_COUNT] = { 0 }; // input without rotation gain

                  float D[CARTESIAN_COORDINATE_POSE_COUNT / 2 * MAX_FINGER_COUNT] = { 0 }; // input without rotation gain

                  float I[CARTESIAN_COORDINATE_POSE_COUNT / 2 * MAX_FINGER_COUNT] = { 0 }; // input without rotation gain

                  float iLimit[CARTESIAN_COORDINATE_POSE_COUNT / 2 * MAX_FINGER_COUNT] = { 0 }; // input without rotation gain

                  for (int i = 0; i < CARTESIAN_COORDINATE_POSE_COUNT / 2 * MAX_FINGER_COUNT; i++)

                  {

                                    P[i] = 5;

                                    D[i] = 12;

                                    I[i] = 0.012;

                                    ILimit[i] = 0.1;

                  }

                  DG_RESULT result = SetManipulationGainPIDAll(P, D, I, ILimit);

Appendix 1. Glossary and Description

B                     

Baudrate

The data transfer rate, where the unit of data transfer is baud.

Blend list

A collection of lists for continuous positional Motions with recipe poses and recipe gains.

Blend motion

A Motion with a saved blend list.

Blend move

Actuates a list of blends consisting of recipe poses and recipe gains in a continuous loop in the order they are registered.

C                    

Cartesian coordinate

 A coordinate system that mathematically describes the position of a point in 3D space, consisting of the x-, y-, and z-axes. Cartesian coordinate system.

Communication Period

 Time to send and receive data between devices.

COMPORT

 The input and output ports on the computer used for serial communication.

D                    

Developer Mode

 A mode that uses a user-developed controller, which receives information from each joint of the gripper and allows you to control each joint directly.

E         

Encoder

 A sensor that outputs information about the position and velocity of an object in rotational or linear motion as an electrical signal.

 

F                      

Fix tilt option (Fix tilt grasp option)

Gripper The ability to perform a grasp action with the tilt of the 4th joint of the finger maintained relative to the current pose when executing a grasp action with this option.

I            

In-hand manipulation

 Control functions to manipulate the position and orientation of objects held by the robot hand.

Inpose

When moving from position control to a target joint position value, the range to verify that the target position value has been reached. This is often used to perform other motions before reaching the target position due to the infose value.

J                      

Joint

A drive unit with a 1 degree of freedom rotation axis. For the Delto Gripper series, the DG-3F has 12 joints, the DG-4F has 18 joints, and the DG-5F has 20 joints.

L         

Low Pass Filter

 A filter that passes below a certain frequency, reducing noise in the received digital signal and smoothing out abrupt changes to produce a smoother result.

M                  

Modbus protocol (Modbus protocol)

 An industry-standard communication protocol developed for communication between automation devices that uses a master-slave structure and supports a variety of communication methods, including RTU, ASCII, and TCP/IP. Connected devices can be identified through Slave IDs.

Modbus RTU (Modbus RTU)

It is a protocol based on serial communication, such as RS-232 or RS-485, and uses a binary format for efficient and fast communication.

Modbus TCP (Modbus TCP)

A Modbus protocol that operates on top of TCP/IP networks. It transmits data in the form of packets and allows for fast and flexible communication over a network.

Module

 Minimum actuation unit divided into independent parts. The Delto Gripper series consists of one independent module for each joint, allowing for independent operation, scalability and ease of maintenance. Each module consists of a motor, encoder, motor drive, reducer, etc.

O       

Operator Mode

Mode controlled using a controller inside the product. Mode that supports the Modbus Protocol and allows you to easily control the gripper by simply changing the register map, or by using the UI operations provided.

Overshoot

 A temporary exceedance of a target value in a control system as it converges to the target value.

P                     

Parallel option (Parallel grasp option)

 Unlike the tilt-fixed grasp option, this option always grasps with the planes of the fingertips touching, regardless of the gripper's current pose, to  the contact area with the object when grasping.

PD control (PD control)

A feedback control system that combines proportional and derivative control. By combining a response proportional to the error with a response based on the rate of change of the error, fast and stable control is possible, but perfect error compensation is difficult.

PID control (PID control)

A feedback control system that combines proportional, integral, and derivative control. It is used in automation and robotics systems to achieve desired target values, allowing for stable and precise control.

Position control

 A control method that adjusts the position of a motor or machine part. Moving to a target position based on the current position is called position control, and it can be precisely controlled with PID control.

R        

Recipe

A set of pre-saved data with key settings for easy and efficient control of a robot (gripper). Recipes can be saved in advance to facilitate control through stored recipes.

 

S                     

Smooth grasping (Smooth grasping mode)

 A uses a weak grasp to avoid damaging the object when grasping itthe set grasp strength after contacting the object.

Socket communication

 How two devices send and receive data over a network. IP addresses, PORT numbers identify the devices to send and receive.

Software Development Kit (SDK)

A collection of tools and libraries for developing software applications. Users can utilize the SDK to easily implement functionality for gripper control.

T        

TCP/IP

 A core protocol for internet and network communications that allows data to be reliably delivered. LAN ports allow for wired network connectivity and efficient connection of multiple devices.

W    

Window Socket API (WSA)

 An API that supports socket programming on Windows operating systems, enabling data communication between a client and a server.
